clue.text: He is in Manchester metropolitan area

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: the letters HE sit in the very middle of the word Manchester, between MANC and STER, so HE is that word's central pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A city's downtown core is its central district, the heart of the metropolitan area.

clue.text: One in boat heard birds

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the cox steers a rowing boat

explanation.surface: Someone sitting in a boat hears birds calling.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocks are male birds, especially male domestic fowl.

clue.text: Raised objection to firm sacking us, needing to slim down from this state?

definitions.text: needing to slim down from this state?

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

indicators.note: sacking means getting rid of, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a business is a firm

explanation.surface: Staff protest at a company laying them off, as if the firm were slimming down.
explanation.walkthrough: BUT turned upward gives TUB; BUSINESS without US leaves BINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubbiness is plumpness, a condition from which a dieter would want to lose weight.

clue.text: Caution criminal: cops in crime cut

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are wrongly arranged, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police caution: officers' crime-fighting budgets have been slashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caution' reads like the formal police warning, which fits the cops in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Circumspection is wariness, care taken before acting, the same as caution.

clue.text: Cask overturned? Enclose one that's cracked

indicators.note: overturned means the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer
to case is to enclose in a casing

explanation.surface: A barrel has been knocked over; seal up the one that has split.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracked is slang for crazy, and a nutcase is a crazy person.

clue.text: Family members must be told

definitions.meaning: people in the same family are connected by kinship
a story that has been narrated or recounted

explanation.surface: Relatives have to be informed, perhaps of some family news.
explanation.definitionFit: Kin are connected by blood, and an account that has been recounted has been narrated.

clue.text: Fancy woman draped round head of Eton

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped around another like cloth hung over it

parts.note: Ida is a woman's name

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman wraps herself around an Old Etonian she has taken a fancy to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective or a verb about the woman; it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, as a noun, is a notion or whimsical thought conjured by the imagination.

clue.text: Police officer seizes stolen loincloth

indicators.note: the officer grabs and holds the next piece inside

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A detective arrests someone with a stolen garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a long cloth wrapped round the waist and legs, worn by men in India.

clue.text: After training a bold man I like tummy muscles

definitions.note: plural, while the entry is singular: one abdominal is one of these stomach muscles

indicators.note: training puts something into a new shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone admires the toned stomach of a bold man who has been working out.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominals are the muscles of the abdomen, the stomach wall that gym training aims to tone.

clue.text: Hindu festival-then author turned sanctimonious

parts.note: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours

indicators.note: turned means the letters are changed round into a new order

explanation.surface: After a religious festival, a writer becomes self-righteous.
explanation.definitionFit: A holier-than-thou attitude is a smug, morally superior one, which is what sanctimonious means.

clue.text: Show Spartan having whip-round?

indicators.note: the whip goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip, is called the cat for short
spartan means austere, bare of comforts

explanation.surface: A person of Spartan habits takes part in a whip-round, a collection of money among colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' reads as one word for a collection; split it, and 'round' becomes the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a show of songs, dances and sketches staged in a nightclub or restaurant.

clue.text: King and pope asked for opinions on the radio

parts.note: Leo is a name taken by thirteen popes

indicators.note: radio is heard, not read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to poll people is to ask them for their opinions

explanation.surface: A monarch and a pontiff are canvassed for their views in a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Leopold was the name of several monarchs, notably kings of the Belgians.

clue.text: Double sulphate brought back in time worked as a pick-me-up

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a stint is a spell of time spent working

indicators.note: brought back means the word is turned round, read from its end

parts.note: alum is a double sulphate of aluminium and potassium

explanation.surface: A chemical compound returned in time acted as a tonic, like a dose of smelling salts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' looks like the verb before 'as a pick-me-up'; it belongs with 'time', a spell on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulant is something that raises energy or alertness, which is what a tonic or reviver does.

clue.text: Oddly neglected Bird Man, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are ignored, keeping the even ones

parts.note: the Isle of Man is abbreviated IOM

explanation.surface: A bird-loving man, rather overlooked, speaks in his own peculiar way.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first and third letters of Bird leaves its second and fourth, I and D.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression peculiar to a language, a characteristic turn of phrase.

clue.text: Experts ringing right trees

indicators.note: the experts surround the other letter like a ring

parts.note: aces are experts, top performers

explanation.surface: Specialists encircle the correct trees, perhaps arborists at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Acers are maples, the genus of trees named Acer in botany.

clue.text: A large flier? Explorer follows another

indicators.note: the explorer comes after the preceding pieces

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
a bat is a flying mammal
Sir James Clark Ross was a British polar explorer

explanation.surface: A big bird or plane, then an explorer comes after another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A large flier?' looks like the definition; it is wordplay, and 'another' (another large flier) is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The albatross is itself a very large flier, a seabird with the longest wingspan of any bird.

clue.text: Fat person losing second home gets painkiller

indicators.note: the second piece is taken away from the first

parts.note: an endomorph is a person with a heavy, rounded build
a mo is a moment, a second
in means at home

explanation.surface: An overweight person who loses their second home gets something for the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is not an ordinal here but MO, a brief moment, taken out of ENDOMORPH to leave ENDORPH.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorphins are hormones made in the brain that relieve pain naturally.

clue.text: Has old-fashioned artist taken up a system to promote wellbeing?

parts.note: hath is the archaic form of has

indicators.note: in a down entry, taken up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Goya was a Spanish painter

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned artist has adopted a regime for staying healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatha yoga is the physical form of yoga, with postures and breathing for health.

clue.text: Belfries designed to house a work of art

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
designed means arranged into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bell towers built to accommodate a sculpture or painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Bas-relief is sculpture carved so it stands only slightly out from its background, an artwork.

clue.text: Craftsman admitted heading for London with philosopher

parts.note: admitted means let in

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: An artisan, once admitted, heads for London with a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlayer is a craftsman who sets pieces of wood, metal or stone into a surface.

clue.text: Mere stranger introduced by supporter as an honoured citizen

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are brought into the middle of the supporter

parts.note: a fan is a supporter

indicators.note: stranger here means more strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mere stranger is presented by a backer as a distinguished resident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a noun for an outsider; it is a comparative adjective signalling that MERE becomes REEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeman is a person given the freedom of a city, an honour granted to distinguished citizens.

clue.text: Golf follower in Fawlty Towers, say

definitions.meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word after Golf (G) is the one for H
Fawlty Towers, a British TV sitcom, is set in a guest house in Torquay

explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf follower' suggests a golf fan; it is the phonetic alphabet's word after Golf. 'in' just joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the NATO code word for H, and an establishment offering rooms to guests.

clue.text: Upright character taken into consideration — that's understood

indicators.note: the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: tact is consideration for others' feelings
the letter I is a single upright stroke

explanation.surface: A morally upright person is given proper consideration, a point that goes without saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright character' sounds like a person of integrity; it is the letter I, drawn as a single vertical stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit describes something implied or understood without being stated.

clue.text: Crop left for fawn

parts.note: a bird's crop, the pouch in its gullet, is also called the craw

explanation.surface: A farmer leaves a harvest for a young deer to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fawn' looks like the young deer; it is the verb, to grovel.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to be obsequious, and to crawl is to grovel in the same way.

clue.text: Leave your pit later and hold your horses, as some bushwhackers do

parts.note: to stay in bed longer than usual, pit being slang for bed, is a lie-in
hold your horses means wait, be patient

explanation.surface: Advice to sleep late and be patient, as ambushers waiting in the bush would.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushwhackers ambush travellers, hiding and waiting to attack by surprise.

clue.text: River that's appreciated by good American

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
US stands for American, of the United States

explanation.surface: A river that a good American would enjoy visiting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus is the longest river of the Iberian peninsula, reaching the sea at Lisbon.

clue.text: Old party member with god in chapel

indicators.note: the god goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A veteran politician with God at his side, at prayer in a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratory is a small chapel used for private prayer.

clue.text: Nursemaid missing first run packs new game

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: an amah is a nursemaid in East and South Asia

indicators.note: the run holds the next letter packed inside it

parts.note: to jog is to run at a gentle pace

explanation.surface: A nanny, absent from the opening run, packs up a new game for the children.
explanation.definitionFit: Mah-jong is a Chinese game played with tiles, usually by four players.

clue.text: Only popular music in recital

indicators.note: a recital is spoken aloud, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: soul is a genre of popular music

explanation.surface: A concert programme made up of nothing but pop songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recital' suggests a concert; here it signals that the word is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means single, one and no other, as in the sole survivor.

clue.text: Argonauts gathered round Jason finally discovering arboreal creatures

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the next piece
gathered suggests the letters are brought together in a new arrangement
finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: The heroic crew of the Argo assemble around their leader Jason and come upon tree-dwelling animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Orang-utans are great apes of Borneo and Sumatra that live mostly in the treetops.
